title: Late Fees on Ridgeline Home Improvement Financing Accounts and How Far Behind the Account Stands
content:
Collections desk guidance for Ridgeline Home Improvement Financing, applying to late fees on accounts whose plan carries no promotion (a fixed-rate or low-payment plan).

**Rule.** How the fixed late fee and the share figure are combined follows how far behind the account stands on the assessment date, counting as payments behind the scheduled payments that have fallen due (one for each statement period that carries a monthly-interest entry, less the months deferred under hardship deferrals) minus the whole scheduled payments covered by scheduled-payment entries net of returned payments: two or more payments behind takes the higher of the fixed late fee and the share figure; fewer than two payments behind, on an account that has never left a late fee standing unreversed and has never had a payment returned, takes the share figure alone; every other account takes the lower of the two. An account paid ahead of its schedule counts as no scheduled payments behind.

## Definitions

- **Scheduled payments fallen due**: the number of statement periods on the account carrying a monthly-interest entry, less the months deferred under every hardship deferral on the account.
- **Whole scheduled payments covered**: the money posted as scheduled-payment entries less the money of returned payments, divided by the scheduled payment and rounded down to a whole number.
- **Payments behind**: fallen due less covered; an account paid ahead of its schedule, where covered exceeds fallen due, counts as none behind.
- **Never left a late fee standing unreversed**: over the life of the account, the late-fee entries less the late-fee reversals come to zero or fewer.
- **Never had a payment returned**: no returned payment over the life of the account.

## Combination table

| Payments behind | Late fee left standing ever, or payment returned ever | Combination |
|---|---|---|
| 2 or more | Either | The higher of the fixed late fee and the share figure |
| 0 or 1 | Neither | The share figure alone |
| 0 or 1 | At least one of them | The lower of the fixed late fee and the share figure |

## Hypothetical cases

- 9 periods carry a monthly-interest entry, no deferral, 6 whole payments covered: 3 behind, so the higher of the two.
- 9 periods, a deferral of 2 months, 6 whole payments covered: 1 behind; one returned payment on record, so the lower of the two.
- 5 periods, 4 whole payments covered, no late fee ever left standing and no return: 1 behind, so the share figure alone.
